summary: Wi-Fi AP multicast snooping drops mDNS/LLMNR over ZeroTrust VPN causing internal service discovery failures
description:
Issue summary:
Users in the San Francisco office intermittently lose connectivity to internal developer services (git, CI dashboards, kubernetes API) immediately after roaming between Wi-Fi APs. Connections appear to fail service discovery (git-server.example.internal, registry-svc.local) rather than DNS resolution for public sites. Impact: several engineering teams report failed git pushes, inability to list pods via kubectl, and flaky service-to-service name lookups when on corporate Wi-Fi and connected through the ZeroTrust agent VPN.

Impact:
- Affected ~15 engineers across multiple teams since 2026-03-10 09:00 PDT.
- Symptoms: "git push" stalls with SSH timeout or fails with "could not resolve hostname git-server.example.internal"; kubectl returns "No resources found" or times out when targeting in-cluster services by name.

Environment:
- Corporate Wi-Fi (APs managed by ACME Wireless controller) using VLAN-per-SSID and client isolation off.
- ZeroTrust agent (v2.8.1) performing split-tunnel + forced internal routes.
- VPN gateway cluster (us-west-1) handling ZeroTrust tunnels.
- Internal name resolution relies on LLMNR/mDNS for some legacy service discovery and conditional DNS forwarding for *.internal zones.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Connect Macbook (macOS 13.6) to corp-employee-5g SSID.
2) Authenticate via 802.1X (Okta SAML) and allow ZeroTrust agent to start.
3) Move ~20 meters to trigger roaming to an adjacent AP.
4) Attempt to resolve or use service names that are discovered via mDNS/LLMNR (e.g., git-server.example.internal, registry-svc.local).
5) Observe failed name resolution or service discovery; public DNS (google.com) remains reachable.

Observed behavior:
- After roaming, mDNS/LLMNR traffic is intermittently blocked; we see no mDNS announcements from the hosts on the same VLAN when captured on the AP.
- ZeroTrust logs show repeated link re-registration, but successful tunnel re-establishment.
- Wireless controller shows "multicast-snooping: enabled" on several APs and a recent firmware push on 2026-03-09.

Expected behavior:
- Roaming should preserve multicast discovery frames inside the office VLAN or ZeroTrust agent should fallback to DNS-based discovery. Service name resolution should remain stable across AP handoffs.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent AP firmware (2026-03-09) introduced more aggressive multicast snooping/IGMP proxy behavior that suppresses mDNS/LLMNR broadcast flooding across uplinks during client roaming, causing discovery packets to be dropped between clients and edge service proxies. ZeroTrust agent split-tunnel routing expects the multicast traffic to be available locally and does not re-issue DNS queries to conditional forwards when discovery fails.

Relevant logs/metrics/links:
- Wireless controller event stream: https://acme-wireless.console/company/events?id=EVT-20260309-472
- ZeroTrust agent logs (anonymized) attached in comments.
- Packet capture (pcap) from AP before/after roam: stored on /mnt/support_pcaps/INT-856123/pcap_pair.zip
- Slack thread: #netops -> https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0NETOPS/p1640001234567
steps_to_reproduce: Connect to corp-employee-5g SSID and authenticate
Trigger AP roaming by walking between AP coverage zones
Attempt to resolve mDNS/LLMNR-hosted service names
Observe resolution failures while public internet remains reachable
comments: 2026-03-10 09:34 - Liam Chen: Acknowledged. I've pulled the AP event stream and firmware audit. Assigning to network team for initial triage.
2026-03-10 11:12 - Priya Rao (NetOps): Confirmed firmware 5.4.2 was pushed 2026-03-09 to 8 APs in SF. Multicast snooping defaults changed in that release. Collecting PCAPs now.
2026-03-10 13:45 - Support: Customer-impacting. Raising P1. Notifying affected teams via #eng-oncall.

2026-03-11 08:20 - Liam Chen: From PCAPs, mDNS queries are seen from client but no responses appear after roam; IGMP membership reports are not forwarded across the AP uplink intermittently. Suspect snooping on APs is not learning multicast groups during fast roam.

2026-03-12 10:02 - Priya Rao: As a mitigation test, we've disabled 'fast-snooping' on two APs in SF and observed service discovery recovered for two test clients during roaming. Scheduling a controlled rollback to previous firmware on remaining APs tonight.

2026-03-13 09:57 - Liam Chen: ZeroTrust logs show agent re-registers 3x on roam; suggest adding a short retry/backoff for conditional DNS lookup fallback until multicast stability is verified. Opening INT-856124 to track ZeroTrust agent change request.
2026-03-13 11:30 - Priya Rao: Rollback completed on 6/8 APs; monitoring. Early metrics show reduction in discovery failures from 18/hour to ~1/hour on affected SSID.
2026-03-13 16:05 - Maya Patel: Affected engineers report improvement. Leaving ticket in progress while we complete full rollback and validation across other sites.
investigation_notes: PCAP analysis: client mDNS queries present; AP uplink suppresses multicast frames post-roam; IGMP reports not propagated.
Wireless controller config diff shows 'fast-snooping' flag introduced in 5.4.2 that reduces IGMP query forwarding during client handoffs.
Reproduced locally on a lab Macbook with 802.1X and ZeroTrust agent: enabling fast-snooping causes 60-90s discovery blackhole during roam.
Workaround validated: disable fast-snooping on APs or perform firmware rollback to 5.4.1; both restored expected behavior.
ZeroTrust agent could implement a fallback to conditional DNS forwarders when mDNS/LLMNR discovery fails but that requires product change and release coordination.
resolution: Mitigation: rolled back AP firmware on affected units (6/8), disabled 'fast-snooping' where needed. Service discovery restored in monitored zones. Next steps: complete rollback to 5.4.1 across SF campus, open product ticket for ZeroTrust agent to add DNS fallback (INT-856124). Post-incident: recommend vendor firmware hold until multicast behavior validated in lab.
follow_up_actions: Complete firmware rollback on remaining APs in SF by 2026-03-14
Coordinate with Wireless vendor to revert default behavior in future builds
Work with ZeroTrust product team to scope DNS-fallback feature (INT-856124)
Add synthetic service-discovery checks to Redwood Console network health dashboards
